Twelve-Angled Stone

Twelve corners in a living city street

Current ratingsOpening hoursView the place on the map
Nearby places

Explore

A single block in the wall on Hatun Rumiyoc is famous for its twelve corners. The surrounding stones matter just as much: each joint changes direction to fit the neighbouring block. This is a working pedestrian street, so study it from one side.

Planning your visit

15–25 min · Allow this time for the visit itself. Add travel, admission queues and any scheduled tour separately.

What to look for

Twelve corners in a living city street

Start counting at a clearly visible corner and follow the joint in one direction. Give other pedestrians room to pass; the best photograph often comes from waiting for a gap, not moving closer.

Getting there

History and local experience

Counting corners is only a first step. Follow a line of joints past the famous block to see how the same method connects stones of quite different shapes along the street.

Walking route

  1. Calle Hatun Rumiyoc, Cusco
  2. Enter Hatun Rumiyoc from the centre, locate the signed block and trace its edges with your eyes.
  3. Continue to the far end of the wall to compare a different set of joints without touching the stone.
